key_insight: MoRight disentangles object motion control from camera viewpoint and enforces motion causality so user-specified actions produce physically coherent reactions (not just pixel displacements) under freely chosen views.
problem_solved: Generating motion-controlled videos that allow separate control of object actions and camera viewpoint while ensuring actions cause coherent, plausible responses in other scene elements.
method: Learn disentangled latent factors for object motion and camera viewpoint so users can independently control action and view.
Introduce a causal dynamics / interaction module that predicts how user-driven actions propagate to other objects, ensuring reactionary behavior instead of pixel-level copying.
Train end-to-end with view-consistency and action-conditioned supervision (multi-view or rendering-aware constraints) to maintain physical plausibility across arbitrary viewpoints.
impact: Makes controllable, physically-plausible video generation practical for animation, simulation, data augmentation, and robotics, enabling users to specify actions and viewpoints reliably. Practitioners gain a tool for interpretable control and realistic interaction modeling in generated video.
visual_elements: Schematic showing disentangled latents: separate sliders/icons for 'Action' and 'Camera' controlling the generation pipeline
Before vs after examples: baseline (entangled/ pixel-shift) vs MoRight (causal reactions) showing interacting objects
Interaction graph / causal flow diagram illustrating how an action on one object triggers predicted reactions in others
Viewpoint montage: same action rendered from multiple camera angles to highlight view-consistency
paper_authors: Shaowei Liu, Xuanchi Ren, Tianchang Shen, Huan Ling, Saurabh Gupta
